questions.question: What is the main purpose of Configuration Management in a complex project, like building a robot or a detailed computer program?

options.A: To make sure the project is finished as quickly as possible, even if some details are missed.
options.B: To keep track of all the parts, plans, and changes so everyone on the team always works with the correct and latest versions.
options.C: To decide which team member gets to build the most important or difficult parts of the project.
options.D: To only focus on the final testing phase, ignoring how the project was put together.

questions.explanation: Configuration Management is about maintaining order, understanding what you have, and carefully managing any changes throughout your project's lifecycle, ensuring your creation remains coherent and functional.

questions.question: In Creationeering, what does a 'baseline' represent in a project?

options.A: The very first rough sketch or idea you have for your project.
options.B: A list of all the tools and materials you will need to begin building.
options.C: A formally agreed-upon snapshot of your project's design or configuration at a specific point in time, used as a trusted reference.
options.D: The final step of verifying that your completed creation works perfectly.

questions.explanation: A baseline is a formally agreed-upon snapshot of a system's configuration at a specific point in time, serving as a reference point for future changes and development.

questions.question: Why is 'Change Control' an essential part of Configuration Management for maintaining a system's integrity?

options.A: It allows anyone on the team to make changes to the design whenever they think it's a good idea.
options.B: It ensures that all requests for changes are carefully evaluated, approved, tracked, and implemented in an organized way.
options.C: It helps the team remember the initial goals of the project before any work begins.
options.D: It is only necessary for very small and simple projects where few changes are expected.

questions.explanation: Change Control is the process of managing all requests for changes to a system's configuration, including evaluating, approving, tracking, and implementing those changes in a structured way to maintain integrity.

questions.question: How does God's creation in Genesis 1 connect to the concept of establishing baselines in our Creationeering projects?

options.A: God created everything randomly, showing that strict baselines are not always needed for creation.
options.B: God established a clear, ordered, and functional state for each phase of creation, declaring it 'good,' which served as a stable baseline for the next step.
options.C: God's creation was so perfect that He didn't need to manage any changes or configurations after the initial act.
options.D: The Bible only talks about creation, not about managing ongoing projects or changes.

questions.explanation: The lesson explains that God's declaration of 'good' after each phase of creation signifies a completed, stable, and acceptable configuration for that stage, acting as a baseline for the next step.

questions.question: In the Creationeering framework, why is Configuration Management especially important during the 'Assembly phase' of a project?

options.A: Because the Assembly phase is when you decide on the very first design ideas and requirements.
options.B: Because once parts start coming together, many changes can happen, and it's easy for things to get messy without careful tracking and management.
options.C: Because Configuration Management is only about verifying and validating the design before any building starts.
options.D: Because it's the only time you need to think about what specific tools and equipment you'll use.

questions.explanation: The lesson states that Configuration Management fits the Assembly phase because 'once parts start coming together, things can get messy fast,' and a small change to one piece can affect many others, requiring careful tracking.

questions.question: In Configuration Management, what is a 'Configuration Item' (CI)?

options.A: Any component, document, or part of a system that needs to be managed and tracked.
options.B: Only the final assembled product of a project.
options.C: A temporary note or idea that is not officially part of the design.
options.D: The person responsible for approving all changes.

questions.explanation: A Configuration Item is any part of a system, including hardware, software, or documents, that requires careful management and tracking.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of 'Version Control' in Configuration Management?

options.A: To track and manage changes to files and documents over time, allowing for comparison and reversion.
options.B: To formally approve all proposed changes to a project's baseline.
options.C: To check if the physical product matches the documented design.
options.D: To define the initial stable state of a project.

questions.explanation: Version Control specifically tracks modifications to items over time, enabling users to see changes and revert to older states if needed.

questions.question: When we talk about 'traceability' in Creationeering projects, what does it allow us to do?

options.A: To quickly build new parts without documentation.
options.B: To track the history, application, or location of an item or activity.
options.C: To decide the best color for a robot's exterior.
options.D: To ignore past mistakes and only focus on the future.

questions.explanation: Traceability provides the ability to follow the entire history of a component or action, understanding who did what, when, and why.

questions.question: Your Creationeering team is designing a new water filter. Which of these would most likely be designated as a Configuration Item (CI) for your project?

options.A: The specific type of filter membrane material used in the design.
options.B: The brand of pencils used for sketching ideas.
options.C: The song playing in the background during a design meeting.
options.D: The empty snack wrapper from lunch.

questions.explanation: The filter membrane is a critical component of the design that needs to be managed and tracked, making it a Configuration Item.

questions.question: A Creationeering team has developed several different software codes for controlling their robot's arm. They want to experiment with a new code, but also need to be able to quickly switch back to any of the previous working codes if the new one doesn't perform well. Which Configuration Management practice would best help them do this?
questions.explanation: Version Control allows teams to track different versions of code, compare them, and easily revert to a previous working version.

questions.question: After completing the assembly of their solar-powered car, the Creationeering team wants to verify that every part installed matches the approved design documents and parts list. What specific Configuration Management activity should they perform?

options.A: Creating a new baseline for the finished car.

questions.explanation: A Configuration Audit is a formal check to ensure that the physical product matches its documented configuration.

questions.question: How does the comprehensive practice of Configuration Management, including tracking changes and maintaining order in our projects, connect to the biblical principle of stewardship?

options.A: It shows that we should avoid making any changes to our creations once they are started.
options.B: It demonstrates responsible and diligent management of the resources, designs, and work entrusted to us.
options.C: It suggests that God's creation was chaotic and required constant, unplanned adjustments.
options.D: It encourages us to keep all project information secret from others.

questions.explanation: Configuration Management reflects stewardship by promoting careful, orderly, and accountable management of all aspects of a project, honoring the gifts and responsibilities given to us.

questions.question: Which of the following are key reasons why Configuration Management is important in a Creationeering project? (Select all that apply.)

options.A: To make sure the project is finished as quickly as possible.
options.B: To keep track of all parts, plans, and changes.
options.C: To ensure everyone on the team always uses the correct and latest versions.
options.D: To only focus on the final testing phase of the project.

questions.explanation: Configuration Management's main purpose is to maintain order by tracking all project elements and changes, ensuring the team works with up-to-date and accurate information.

questions.question: In a Creationeering project, which of these would most likely be considered a Configuration Item (CI) that needs careful management? (Select all that apply.)

options.A: The specific type of motor chosen for a robot arm.
options.B: A temporary sketch on a napkin that hasn't been approved.
options.C: The official blueprint document showing how all parts fit together.
options.D: The color of the paint used on the workshop walls.

questions.explanation: A Configuration Item is any component or document that is a crucial part of the system and needs to be managed and tracked throughout the project.

questions.question: A ___ is a formally agreed-upon snapshot of a project's design at a specific point in time, and any changes to it must go through a process called ___.
questions.explanation: A baseline provides a stable reference point for a project, and Change Control is the organized process for managing any modifications to that reference.

questions.question: Put the following steps, which are part of the 'Change Control' process, in the correct order.
questions.explanation: Change Control follows a structured sequence to ensure changes are made responsibly: first understanding the change, then deciding if it should happen, monitoring its progress, and finally putting it into effect.
